audit_findings.title: Parent-share numerator is mixed with consolidated cash-flow components
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 NCI income of $176.8 million and NCI distributions of $226.0 million were 2.56x and 3.27x the $69.1 million absolute anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: OE numerator and per-share denominator are on inconsistent ownership bases
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements of the Company include all assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses of surgical facilities in which the Company has sufficient ownership and rights to allow the Company to consolidate the surgical facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership-basis mismatch is demonstrated, but its net direction is not: consolidated depreciation add-backs may raise OE, while consolidated capex and working-capital charges may lower it. The affected filed amounts are several times anchor OE, so a consistent parent-attributable reconstruction could materially change or eliminate the negative anchor.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year using parent-attributable cash flows, or start with consolidated cash flows and deduct all NCI cash claims consistently; reconcile 2025 specifically to $176.8 million of NCI income and $226.0 million of distributions.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may be operating reinvestment omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 finance-lease asset additions were $31.5 million and principal cash outflows were $39.2 million, equal to 45.6% and 56.7% of absolute anchor OE, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: OE adds back depreciation but may omit the capital charge for operating assets obtained through finance leases
audit_findings.evidence: The Company's finance leases are primarily for medical equipment and information technology and telecommunications assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that finance leases fund operating equipment and that the associated principal is outside operating cash flow. If neither lease additions nor principal were charged, OE is overstated. Either filed measure is large relative to the $69.1 million anchor; they are alternative measures and must not be added together. The parent-attributable and normalized amount remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate OE with one consistent finance-lease capital charge—asset additions or operating-asset principal—and reconcile it to lease amortization, the $935.5 million year-end liability, and NCI ownership without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The model compounds a negative anchor and reverses scenario meaning
audit_findings.magnitude: computed: BULL is $2.66 per share below BEAR, and BASE is $702.0 million or $5.34 per share below a zero common-equity floor
audit_findings.mechanism: growth formula and terminal value compound negative OE; the equity-value output lacks an economically appropriate limited-liability treatment
audit_findings.evidence: We had net losses attributable to Surgery Partners, Inc. of $77.9 million, $168.1 million and $11.9 million, in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model error: increasing growth from negative OE enlarges losses, producing BULL at negative $6.61 per share versus BEAR at negative $3.95. Perpetual negative cash flows also create negative common-equity values even though shareholders ordinarily cannot be compelled to fund them. The numerical scenario conclusion is therefore not economically interpretable, although the too-hard conclusion remains supported.
audit_findings.action: Route negative OE to an explicit turnaround, liquidation, or unvalued/too-hard branch; verify scenario ordering and apply the documented common-equity floor before presenting any value or buy-below figure.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include cash unavailable to parent common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: computed maximum questioned bridge amount: $216.7 million or $1.65 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: bridge adds consolidated cash without legal-entity, NCI, restriction, or minimum-operating-cash adjustments
audit_findings.evidence: Some of our subsidiaries may become subject to agreements that restrict the sale of assets and significantly restrict or prohibit the payment of dividends or the making of distributions, loans or other payments to stockholders, partners or members.
audit_findings.explanation: No unavailable amount is demonstrated. Even removing the entire $216.7 million add-back—the maximum possible effect—would move BASE from negative $5.34 to approximately negative $6.99 per share and would not change the present negative/too-hard conclusion. A smaller restricted or NCI-owned portion necessarily has less effect.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a legal-entity cash schedule before any post-turnaround rerun and identify restricted, NCI-owned, trapped, and minimum operating cash; no current conclusion change is required.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI creates a contingent cash claim absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed redeemable-NCI carrying balance was $366.7 million at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: a regulatory trigger could create a bridge cash outflow while simultaneously increasing the parent's ownership of facility earnings
audit_findings.evidence: In the event we are required to purchase all of the physicians’ ownership, our existing capital resources would not be sufficient for us to meet this obligation.
audit_findings.explanation: The contingent redemption mechanism is demonstrated, but management assessed the triggering event as remote and no current cash obligation or contractual purchase amount is established. Deducting the carrying balance mechanically would also omit the incremental earnings interest acquired. This is therefore a forward-looking downside item rather than a presently demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor regulatory triggers and obtain the partnership redemption formulas; if trigger probability becomes non-remote, model expected cash consideration and the acquired earnings interest together in a downside scenario.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 controlling-interest acquisition spending was $162.1 million, 2.35x absolute anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: growth and OE reinvestment may include acquired earnings without the associated acquisition cash outlay or financing
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we acquired a controlling interest in twelve surgical facilities and several physician practices and other ancillary businesses for aggregate cash consideration of $162.1 million, net of cash acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: Acquisition spending is demonstrated, but dependence of the forecast on acquisitions is not. Filed same-facility revenue grew 4.9% in 2025 and 4.9% in the first half of 2026, so the 2% base and 5% bull revenue-like rates could potentially be achieved organically; however, revenue growth does not establish OE growth. If acquisitions are necessary, excluding normalized purchase consideration would overstate value materially.
audit_findings.action: Bridge historical revenue and OE growth between same-facility operations, acquisitions, and divestitures; then rerun only if forecast OE growth requires acquisitions, charging normalized purchase consideration and its financing explicitly.
